The protected wiring loom means the office is live within an hour of touching down, and just as quickly disconnected when the stretch is done, the crew moves on and the next opening is already waiting.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Utility crew rotations","Urban road openings","Hour-to-live placements","Truck-rotation offices"],"imageAlt":"Complete exterior of the portable office container, 20 x 8 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning along the 20 ft flank."},"20x10":{"h2":"20x10 ft, the standard office, hardened to travel","intro":"The familiar two-hundred-square-foot office rebuilt around movement: lifting interfaces engineered to the unit\'s completed weight, glazing protected for transit, services terminating in a single armoured connection point. Contractors whose projects run in phases across a region relocate it between sites instead of buying twice. What normally suffers in a relocated cabin is the fit-out, and here the fit-out is anchored and shielded from the outset, specifically because relocation is the plan.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Travelling review rooms","Client-facing phase offices","Protected fit-outs","Width that relocates"],"imageAlt":"Wide exterior view of the portable office container, 20 x 12 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning on the 12 ft end wall."},"30x10":{"h2":"30x10 ft, office and store that redeploy together","intro":"The partitioned office-plus-store as a single relocatable body: instruments stay in their lockable rear room during the move, and the whole unit lifts as one sealed piece. The stiffened frame is what makes travelling loaded acceptable, and that capability is the whole difference between this and simply partitioning an ordinary cabin.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Campaign survey teams","Loaded relocations","Instrument rooms in transit","Redeployable stores"],"imageAlt":"Overall view of the portable office container, 30 x 10 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning down the 30 ft side."},"40x8":{"h2":"40x8 ft, the long unit that follows the alignment","intro":"Linear projects advance, and this office advances with them: a forty-foot slim body lifted from chainage to chainage as fronts complete. The length demands proper lifting engineering, and that is precisely what the hardened frame and matched lift points provide. Road and pipeline contractors move it three or four times across a package instead of placing a new cabin at each front, and the protected loom re-terminates at each drop without an electrician rebuilding the connection from scratch at every single drop.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Advancing work fronts","Chainage relocations","Three moves per package","Re-terminating services"],"imageAlt":"Long exterior view of the portable office container, 40 x 8 ft, reinforced lifting points built into each corner along the full 40 ft run."},"40x10":{"h2":"40x10 ft, headquarters that transfer between projects","intro":"A full four-hundred-square-foot project office engineered to serve consecutive projects rather than one: transferred by crane and trailer at each demobilisation, arriving at the next award with its zones, services and fittings intact. The alternative is buying a headquarters at every award and abandoning that embedded value at every project close-out.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Project-to-project transfer","Demobilisation moves","Offices held as plant","Value across awards"],"imageAlt":"Side-on view of the portable office container, 40 x 10 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning across the 40 ft elevation."},"20x20":{"h2":"20x20 ft, the square that splits, moves and rejoins","intro":"The two-piece square with relocation designed into the joint: each half lifts separately on its own reinforced points, travels as a standard load, and rejoins with the sealed floor strip and paired electrical sets re-mating at the new site. Training rooms and control rooms that must exist at each phase of a long programme move this way. Rejoining is a procedure, not an improvisation, because the joint was engineered for its fifth mating, and not merely its first, which is where improvised joints fail.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Two-lift relocations","Re-mating joints","Phase-following control rooms","Programme training squares"],"imageAlt":"Full-length view of the portable office container, 20 x 20 ft, reinforced lifting points built into each corner around the 20 ft square plan."},"40x12":{"h2":"40x12 ft, the largest office we build to move","intro":"Four hundred and eighty square feet engineered for a life of placements: the heaviest unit in this line, and therefore the one where lifting-point engineering and frame stiffening matter most. It is the most office that can follow the work as a single body, and the hardening premium is what keeps it working after the fifth site instead of giving up somewhere around the second.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Long asset rotations","Mine and EPC services","Circulating head offices","Fifth-site durability"],"imageAlt":"Full elevation of the portable office container, 40 x 12 ft, reinforced lifting points built into each corner over the 40 by 12 ft body."}},"small-office-cabin":{"h2":"Small Office Cabin sizes for one to four people","guidanceLine":"Three compact sizes only. Larger floors live on our main office range page.","10x10":{"h2":"10x10 ft, the two-person office in its element","intro":"One hundred square feet arranged for two people who share a task: a security supervisor beside the CCTV desk, a cashier with the records, a doctor with an assistant. This page\'s whole purpose is the compact brief, so the smallest size is its centre of gravity rather than its afterthought. The cabin lands, connects and works the same day, and the nine-foot ceiling keeps a small footprint from feeling like a box. Most buyers here never needed anything larger, and nothing larger is ever pushed at them here.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Two-person duty rooms","CCTV and security desks","Cash and records points","Clinic side rooms"],"imageAlt":"Full side view of the small office cabin, 10 x 10 ft, a single-bay body with one door and one window across the 10 ft wall."},"20x8":{"h2":"20x8 ft, three desks where depth does not exist","intro":"The compact answer for narrow ground: three desks in a row against the long wall, a door at the end, and a footprint that slots beside a gate, along a boundary or behind a showroom. Small teams that outgrew a guard-post-sized room but have no depth to spare step up to this shape and stop there. It shares the slim body of the bigger ranges but is bought here for a different reason: not because the plot is a corridor, but because the team is three people and perfectly honest with itself about staying that way.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Three-desk slim offices","Beside-the-gate teams","Behind-showroom rooms","Small teams, narrow ground"],"imageAlt":"Complete exterior of the small office cabin, 20 x 8 ft, a compact body proportioned for a tight site corner along the 20 ft flank."},"20x10":{"h2":"20x10 ft, the largest office this page will sell you","intro":"Two hundred square feet for four people, and deliberately the ceiling of this range: anything bigger belongs on the main range page with the full nine-size ladder. Kept here because a four-person office is still a small office, and the buyer comparing it with the two smaller sizes is making a compact-office decision, not a site-headquarters decision dressed up small. The fit-out matches the smaller sizes exactly, so growing from the 10x10 to this floor changes the floor area and changes nothing else at all.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Four-person offices","Compact-office ceiling","Growth from two to four","Same fit-out, more floor"],"imageAlt":"The whole small office cabin, 20 x 10 ft, a single-bay body with one door and one window over the 20 ft length."}},"labor-colony":{"h2":"Every labour colony size, and the site each one runs","60x24-gplus1":{"h2":"60x24 ft G+1, 2880 sq ft planned for 58 to 72 workers","intro":"The smallest colony dormitory holds 58 to 72 workers over two floors and usually anchors a compact site with one toilet block beside it. This is the configuration our own costing sheet uses as its reference for the whole cluster, so quotations on it turn around fastest. Because it is the costing reference, its drawings are the most exercised in the library and surprises are rare. The 6,480 square feet list at Rs 43,74,000 ex-GST at the same flat rate every other size uses. Local height clearances are the one item to confirm early, and our drawing pack includes what approvers ask for.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 129 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 90x24 ft G+2, from the stair end on the left, three floors on a 90 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."},"120x24-gplus1":{"h2":"120x24 ft G+1, 5760 sq ft planned for 115 to 144 workers","intro":"The 120 ft two-floor building is the workhorse of large colonies: 115 to 144 workers in one block, long straight rooms that furnish quickly, and a footprint that packs efficiently in rows with fire separation between them. Row spacing and fire separation dimensions for repeat layouts ship with the first quotation as standard. Gate distance and muster areas are marked on the same layout sheet.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 115 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 120x24 ft G+1, from the front left with the end stair, two floors on a 120 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."},"118x30-gplus1":{"h2":"118x30 ft G+1, 7080 sq ft planned for 142 to 177 workers","intro":"The 30 ft wide body changes the internal planning: deeper rooms, wider aisles and space for in-block amenities that the 24 ft buildings push to separate blocks. A pair of these houses a four-hundred-strong workforce on remarkably little land. Where two of these stand together the services spine between them is designed once and shared by both. Water storage for all floors sits on the stair-core roof slab.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 173 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 120x24 ft G+2, from the stair end on the left, three floors on a 120 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."}},"labor-sheds":{"20x10":{"h2":"20x10 ft Labour Shed: 200 sq ft With a Single Bunk Row","intro":"The smallest published shed. Choose this when occupancy is steady and the shed will stand for several months.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x20 ft labour shed in blue-grey cladding, front-left view, two doors spaced along the long wall"},"20x25":{"h2":"20x25 ft Labour Shed: 500 sq ft, Mid-Point Second Exit","intro":"Length is what changes here rather than width. Two exits shorten travel distance in an emergency and give the hall a second cross-flow air path on still days. It is the size we use as the reference plan on the technical drawing, because at 30 ft every control the shed depends on is visible in a single view.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x30 ft labour shed in pearl-grey cladding, front-left view, with a ridge ventilator along the apex"},"20x40":{"h2":"20x40 ft Labour Shed: 800 sq ft, Three Distributed Exits","intro":"The largest published shed and the lowest rate per square foot, because one roof and one slab now cover twice the floor of the 20x20. Beyond this footprint the frame needs a wider clear span, so the shed is engineered and quoted individually rather than taken from the published six.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x40 ft labour shed in graphite cladding, front-left view, with a continuous eaves louvre band"}},"labor-hutments":{"h2":"Every labour hutment size, and the rooms each block gives","60x24-gplus1":{"h2":"60x24 ft G+1, 2880 sq ft planned for 58 to 72 workers","intro":"The small hutment gives two floors of individual rooms for 58 to 72 workers, each room with its own door, window, fan and board. At the hutment rate of Rs 688.50 per square foot, 4,320 square feet amount to Rs 29,74,320 ex-GST. Its room count divides cleanly by common gang sizes, which is why allocation plans on it stay tidy. Passage lighting runs on its own night circuit.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 86 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour hutment, 90x24 ft G+1, from the left corner at the stair end, two floors on a 90 ft footprint in the room-block hutment build."},"90x24-gplus2":{"h2":"90x24 ft G+2, 6480 sq ft planned for 129 to 162 workers","intro":"Three floors of rooms on the 90 ft plinth reach 129 to 162 workers while the plot stays the size of the two-floor block. Panel joints repeat on a fixed module, so a damaged panel swaps rather than condemns a wall. At Rs 679.50 per square foot, its 4,320 square feet total Rs 29,35,440 ex-GST. Spare panels ordered with the block travel with it between sites, insurance that has saved more than one monsoon.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 86 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Prefab labour camp, 90x24 ft G+1, from the left corner at the stair end, two floors on a 90 ft footprint in the bolted panel camp build."},"90x24-gplus2":{"h2":"90x24 ft G+2, 6480 sq ft planned for 129 to 162 workers","intro":"Three panel floors on the 90 ft footprint carry 129 to 162 workers and still dismantle: the third storey bolts to the same module as the first, and the stair tower unbolts into liftable sections. Foundations are pedestal pads rather than a slab, so leaving a site means lifting pads, not breaking concrete, and the ground reinstates in days. Hookup drawings are issued per site, and repeat customers keep the same block numbering across every project.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 115 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Prefab labour camp, 120x24 ft G+1, from the front left with the end stair, two floors on a 120 ft footprint in the bolted panel camp build."},"118x30-gplus1":{"h2":"118x30 ft G+1, 7080 sq ft planned for 142 to 177 workers","intro":"The wide 30 ft camp body earns its width at the services spine: deeper rooms on one side, a full-width utility zone on the other, all still bolted and movable. Its width suits camps that centralise cooking and washing in the block itself rather than in separate service buildings, keeping the site footprint tight. The utility zone takes water heaters and treatment units indoors, which matters in cold-region postings.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 142 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Prefab labour camp, 118x30 ft G+1, from the left corner at the stair end, two floors on the wide 30 ft body in the bolted panel camp build."},"120x24-gplus2":{"h2":"120x24 ft G+2, 8640 sq ft planned for 173 to 216 workers","intro":"The largest camp stacks three 120 ft panel floors for 173 to 216 workers and remains fully demountable, which no other building this size in the cluster offers. Where a mega-project ends and another begins, this block moves whole. Its 8,640 square feet work out at Rs 58,70,880 ex-GST.
